mentions.name: PDFBolt
mentions.description: A PDF generation API for developers: send HTML, a URL, or a template with JSON data and get a PDF back. Targets the routine PDF jobs SaaS products eventually need, such as invoices, reports, certificates, contracts, and labels. Ships with a Node SDK, with a Python SDK and documentation improvements in progress.

mentions.name: PDFBolt
mentions.description: This is a PDF generation API that converts HTML, a URL, or a Handlebars template with JSON data into a PDF, using Playwright under the hood so modern CSS renders correctly. It supports PDF/X-1a and PDF/X-4 print production with ICC color profiles and CMYK conversion (11 color space converters built on PDFBox 3.0), offers an AI template generator that creates a Handlebars template with sample data from a description, and provides a gallery of 38 pre-built templates. Dashboard template management auto-creates drafts on edit, compares any two versions as rendered PDFs, and supports rollback, with an API in progress so coding agents can create and version templates programmatically.
mentions.source_excerpt: Working on PDFBolt (https://pdfbolt.com) - a PDF generation API. You send HTML, a URL, or a Handlebars template with JSON data, get a PDF back. Uses Playwright underneath so modern CSS just works.

mentions.name: PDF Bolt
mentions.description: This is a Chrome-based PDF generation API focused on print production. It handles converting browser-rendered RGB output to CMYK with ICC color profiles inside the generated PDF, and now supports the PDF/X-1a and PDF/X-4 print standards.
mentions.problem: Browsers render everything in RGB, but print requires CMYK with ICC color profiles, and getting that conversion right inside the PDF turned out to be a much deeper problem than expected.
mentions.source_excerpt: A PDF generation API, Chrome-based. Most of my time lately goes into print production - browsers render everything in RGB but print needs CMYK with ICC color profiles, and getting that conversion right inside the PDF turned out to be a much deeper problem than expected. Got PDF/X-1a and PDF/X-4 working now.
